newsitem.title: USA: US urges Zaire's Kabila to cooperate on refugees.
newsitem.headline: US urges Zaire's Kabila to cooperate on refugees.

text.p: The United States called on Zaire's rebel leader Laurent Kabila on Wednesday to cooperate with a U.N. plan to repatriate thousands of Rwandan refugees.

"This is a very serious situation," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said at a briefing. "There have been good promises from Mr. Kabila and his forces, but they have not come through with the action necessary to give the United Nations access to the refugees, and some of those refugees have perished."

The repatriation plan requires Kabila's consent to allow relief workers to get through the rebel-held city of Kisangani to reach some 80,000 refugees situated some 16 to 25 miles (26 to 40 km) south of the city, Burns said.
Kabila's permission is also needed to allow an airlift of refugees to begin, possibly as early as Friday, according to Burns.

"We welcome the cooperation to date given by Mr. Kabila," Burns said. "But we call for urgent approval by him, and consent of this UNHCR (United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees) repatriation plan and the assistance operations so that further deaths and suffering can be prevented and rapid and safe repatriation of the refugees can begin."
Burns also said Washington was "pleased" at the nomination of Etienne Tshisekedi as Zaire's new prime minister on Tuesday.

Once Tshisekedi takes office, Burns said, "we hope that the first order of business for the new Zairean government will be to negotiate an end to the conflict inside Zaire, and to prepare for arrangements for a political transition in Zaire."
